alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not substitute truncation, arithmetic right shift, implicit HDL expression sizing or wraparound for the frozen C02 behavior.
applicability: RTL implementation of the selected C MF16/MTI2/FFT32 and later power/CFAR blocks.
assessed_root_cause: Premature narrowing, arithmetic shifts for negative values or multiple rounding points change numerical results and may alter alarms or peak selection.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Keep full product and accumulator widths through each exact operation; apply mathematical ties-to-even once at the approved boundary; saturate rather than wrap and log pre-narrow values.
generalizable_lesson: Translate the executable numeric contract into explicit HDL widths and explicit signed casts before writing operators; never rely on Verilog sizing defaults.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: Intermediate values could be narrowed or rounded early to simplify RTL, changing the bit-true contract while leaving the final output superficially plausible.
non_applicability: Does not authorize any numeric-format, coefficient, alpha, FFT shift or architecture change.
observable_consequence: C02 fixes exact product/pair/accumulator widths, RNE locations, output formats, shift schedule and saturation telemetry; C03 independently checks rational arithmetic.
observed_problem: MF, MTI and FFT contain products, pair sums and butterfly sums whose full integer widths exceed their stored output widths.
repeatable_validation: Compare each stage and boundary against C03 Fraction oracle and C04 stage capture, including negative half-way RNE, min/max and forced overflow vectors.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: C02 exact formats and [0,1,0,1,1] shifts are immutable without formal engineering change approval.
title: Preserve exact intermediate widths and round only at contract-defined boundaries
